issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) require the Animal name getter and setter to use protected visibility (UML shows protected '# getName()/setName()' and the text explicitly: "implement the name getter and setter with protected visibility"). In the solution, both getName() and setName(...) are declared public (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java: lines 10-16). This contradicts the stated visibility in the specification and UML and may confuse students about the intended access level for these methods.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the getter and setter for name protected in the solution (change public String getName() and public void setName(...) to protected), so the implementation matches the problem text and UML. Alternatively, if public visibility was intended, update the problem statement/UML to state public visibility for these methods to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement indicates a protected constructor for Animal (UML shows '# Animal(String)'). The solution declares the Animal constructor as public (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java: lines 6-8). This conflicts with the UML and may confuse students about the intended constructor visibility for the abstract base class.
issues.suggested_fix: If the UML's protected constructor is intentional, change the Animal constructor in the solution to protected Animal(String name) to match the UML and the intended encapsulation. If a public constructor was intended, update the UML/problem text to specify a public constructor to avoid ambiguity.
